newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rebounds from day's low.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil rebounds from day's low.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rebounded slightly from a midday intraday low, late Tuesday afternoon in active trade as the market looked to the west for support, market sources said.
January gas oil was traded down to a low of $31.95 a barrel early afternoon before it picked up to last trade at $32.20, one broker said.
The market traded to a day's high of $32.65 this morning, he said. January swaps was last quoted at $32.15/$32.30, about 30 cents higher than Monday's late quotes of $31.85/$32.00.
There was little change in the jet/gas oil spread with January talked at $1.20/$1.40 per barrel.
January naphtha was quoted up in thin trade, notionally quoted at $24.00/$24.40 per barrel, up from Monday's offer price of $23.90.
Fuel oil edged up slightly on rumours of a January trade at around $117.75 per tonne. January fuel oil was last quoted at $121.00/$122.50 per tonne.
"Asia is struggling to keep up with the west where prices have risen sharply," one trader said.
Demand from Asia is expected to taper off once the market covers its January requirements as most would be away for the Lunar New Year holidays in February, he said.
January gas oil on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) rose by $8.75 per tonne to close at $222.75 per tonne on Monday. It opened on Tuesday to trade at $224.50, up $1.75 a tonne.
IPE gas oil shot up on forecasts of colder European and U.S. weather.
